indicators.note: one word breaking another splits it open and sits in the gap

blocks.note: the heart of something is its centre
a period is a span of time

explanation.surface: A question about how long a heartbreak lasts, as though grief could be measured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart-breaking' reads as one sad adjective, but the hyphen hides a noun and a verb: the period breaks into the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A centimetre is a unit of length, so it is a measure in the metric system.

blocks.note: taken as written
greed is a selfish desire for more

explanation.surface: A statement that selfishness has been proven to exist.
explanation.definitionFit: Something agreed upon is settled and accepted, as an established fact or arrangement is.

blocks.note: first meaning: short of money
second meaning: beaten with a leather strap

explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor hit' reads like a feeble shot in a game; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Strapped is informal for lacking funds, and it is also the past tense of whipping someone with a belt.

blocks.note: surface reading: an instruction to quit writing words that read the same both ways
setter's reading: the phrase for stopping a car happens itself to read the same backwards and forwards

explanation.surface: An instruction to a wordsmith to quit making palindromes.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the six letters both ways: the phrase meaning to halt is itself a palindrome, which the question mark flags.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull up is to bring a vehicle to a halt, the idiom coming from reining in a horse.

clue.text: Pick conference item for visit again

blocks.note: to reap is to gather or pick a crop
Conference is a popular English variety of pear

explanation.surface: Choosing an agenda item for a return visit to a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Conference is a common British pear variety, so the business meeting is really fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: To reappear is to show up once more, which is what a returning visitor does.

indicators.note: something caught by a phrase is held inside its run of letters

blocks.note: sits across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A bird falling prey to a hunter, as nature intends.
explanation.definitionFit: The tern is a slender seabird related to gulls.

clue.text: Still needing bailing out, rowing crew in craft

indicators.note: bailing out a boat empties it, so the word is emptied of its inside and keeps only its ends

blocks.note: only the outside letters survive the emptying
a racing rowing boat carries a crew of eight

explanation.surface: A rowing eight's boat is still shipping water and needs bailing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' looks like a boat in this nautical scene, but it means skill or cunning.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight is dexterity or cunning, as in sleight of hand, which is a kind of craft.

clue.text: Graduate in son is that incompetent as retail worker

indicators.note: incompetent work is botched, so these letters come out in a muddled order
one part goes in the other, which wraps round it

blocks.note: these nine letters are rearranged
to graduate is to pass, as from one stage to the next

explanation.surface: A parent's complaint that their incompetent graduate son ended up working in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: PASS goes inside the rearranged letters after the third.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop assistant serves customers in a store, so is a worker in retail.

definitions.note: a phrase read as an instruction, two words in the answer

blocks.note: first meaning: serving no purpose
second meaning, split in two: the way to save more is to consume less

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words and it becomes advice for saving; the question mark warns of that whimsical second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Something useless achieves nothing, which is what futile means.

clue.text: Rich, as painter's lovely model could be?

definitions.text: as painter's lovely model could be?

blocks.note: first meaning: comfortably off, in a fortunate position

blocks.clueFragment: as painter's lovely model could be?
blocks.note: second meaning, read literally: a beautiful model posing for a portrait is seated and attractive

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for being well placed is read word by word as a description of an artist's sitter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sitting pretty is in a comfortable, prosperous position, as the wealthy are.

blocks.note: first meaning: alert and quick to respond
second meaning, literal: a footballer in possession has the ball at their feet

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for being alert is taken literally as describing a player in possession.
explanation.definitionFit: On the ball is an idiom for being sharp and attentive.

blocks.note: PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for good
the retort 'far from it' means not at all

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict that a wine is anything but good.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinot is a family of grape varieties and the wines made from them, such as Pinot Noir.

indicators.note: the apostrophe marks a dropped H, as in Cockney speech, so the synonym loses that letter too

blocks.note: hurt means harmed; the spoken form drops its opening H

explanation.surface: A Cockney-voiced line: someone with guns, and somebody hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue writes 'hurt' as a Cockney would say it, and its synonym must lose its H the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: Armed means carrying weapons, so supplied with guns.

clue.text: Topping energy, Argentine leader and I

blocks.note: pep is vigour or energy
Juan Perón was president of Argentina
taken as written

explanation.surface: Boasting that one's energy beats even Argentina's leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topping' reads as a verb meaning beating, but it is a pizza topping.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepperoni is a spicy salami commonly put on pizza as a topping.

clue.text: How medicine may be taken, gulping one drink first

indicators.note: what is gulped is swallowed and ends up inside the swallower

blocks.note: medicine is often taken by mouth
Roman numeral one
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: Instructions for taking medicine, washed down with a drink beforehand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' looks like part of the dosing order, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally means at the start or initially, which is first in time.

indicators.note: something dodgy is not straight, so the letters are not in their proper order

blocks.note: these four letters are rearranged
to conduct is to lead

explanation.surface: An exam run crookedly, the result rigged in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: Settled means decided or agreed firmly, as a fixed date or price is.

clue.text: King nowhere to be seen, Greek lass ordered gifts

indicators.note: something nowhere to be seen has gone, so that letter is dropped
putting letters in order means rearranging them

blocks.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king; this is the letter removed
the letters to be rearranged once the king leaves

explanation.surface: With the king absent, a Greek girl is sent presents.
explanation.definitionFit: Largesse is generous giving of money or presents, so it covers gifts handed out.

indicators.note: one piece coming after the other fixes their order in the word

blocks.note: a bar is a pub
a king is a chess man

explanation.surface: A man arriving after the pub, with a bar snack of nuts in view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' suggests bar snacks, but it means mad; in chess the pieces are called men.
explanation.definitionFit: Barking, short for barking mad, is British slang for crazy, as is nuts.

clue.text: Capital in early stage of development, a nuisance

blocks.note: a plant in bud has not yet flowered
taken as written
a pest is a nuisance

explanation.surface: A city at an early stage of growth is a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: Budapest is the capital city of Hungary.

clue.text: Model in weapon of justice, oath

indicators.note: one part goes in the other, which wraps round it

blocks.note: the sword of justice is the blade held by the figure of Justice
to model clothes is to wear them for display

explanation.surface: A statue of Justice with a model inside her sword, sworn on oath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oath' suggests a court's sworn statement, but here it is a curse.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath can mean a profanity, so a swearword is one.

clue.text: He asked for more meat after starter of offal

indicators.note: a starter is what comes first, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: the first letter
liver is a meat, and offal

explanation.surface: A diner asking for second helpings of offal.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver Twist, the workhouse orphan in Dickens's novel, famously asks 'Please, sir, I want some more.'
explanation.definitionFit: The boy who asked for more gruel is Dickens's Oliver Twist, identified here by his famous request.

clue.text: Brother, one cooking chips, we hear?

indicators.note: what we hear is the sound, not the spelling

blocks.note: a fryer is a pan or person that fries chips

explanation.surface: A monk who works in the kitchen frying chips.
explanation.definitionFit: A friar is a member of a religious order, addressed as Brother.

indicators.note: finally points to the very end, so only the closing letter is kept

blocks.note: something that is mine is meant for me
the last letter

explanation.surface: Troops gathered just before a mine blew up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mine' reads as an explosive, but it is the possessive: what is mine is for me.
explanation.definitionFit: Formed means put together or created, as a team or body is assembled.

blocks.note: first meaning: the point where two lines meet
second meaning, a verb: to go fishing with rod and line

explanation.walkthrough: 'Corner fish' sounds like trapping a fish, but the words are separate meanings; 'fish' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: An angle is where two sides meet, and to angle is to catch fish with a hook and line.

blocks.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good
a deep voice or note is low

explanation.surface: Praise for a polish that is good and has real depth.
explanation.definitionFit: A glow is a steady light or radiance, a shine.

clue.text: Chap having locked up drink in it, brings key

indicators.note: one part goes in the other, which wraps round it
whatever is locked up is shut inside, so it sits within the other word

blocks.note: taken as written; it wraps round everything else
a chap is a man
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A man locked up for drink fetches the key to his cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' suggests a door key in this lock-up scene, but it is an adjective meaning crucial. The drink goes inside the chap, and that whole goes inside the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: A key point is a crucial or significant one, so key means important.

clue.text: Lower digit to eight initially: so it has been entered wrongly

indicators.note: initially points to the start, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone typing has keyed a figure wrongly, reducing a digit down to eight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower digit' reads as reducing a number, but it is a digit on the lower body: a toe.
explanation.definitionFit: Tootsie is a playful word for a toe, and a toe is a digit at the bottom of the body.

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things the wrong way round
one part goes about the other, surrounding it

blocks.note: yes is an emphatic agreement, like certainly
hell is great suffering

explanation.surface: A poet who is certainly thoughtful on the subject of suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: Percy Bysshe Shelley was a major English Romantic poet.
